lead: Miami plumbing deals with heat, humidity, hurricanes, slab homes and aging cast-iron drains. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Miami.
risk: failing cast-iron drains, slab leaks and hurricane and king-tide flooding
risk_short: cast-iron drains, slab leaks and flooding
why: Many Miami homes and condos from the 1950s to 1970s have cast-iron drain lines under the slab that are rotting from the inside. Lining or replacing them is a major job, and slab leaks in supply lines are common too.
Hurricanes and king tides flood low areas and back up sewers. High-rise condos add shared risers and building rules for repairs.
water: Miami-Dade Water and Sewer draws mainly from the Biscayne Aquifer, a shallow limestone aquifer. Water from limestone is hard, though treatment softens it somewhat, and scale still builds up in water heaters and fixtures.
tips: Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
Know your condo's rules before plumbing work.
areas: PipeMend works in Brickell, Downtown, Little Havana, Coconut Grove, Wynwood, Little River, Coral Way and every other Miami neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Miami Building Department, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: Why do older Miami homes have drain problems?
faq.a: Many homes from the 1950s to 1970s have cast-iron drains under the slab. Florida's heat and wastewater corrode them from the inside, causing slow drains, backups and sewer smells. A camera inspection shows whether lining or replacement is needed.
